subject: botany
question_text: Write the role of fungi in daily life.

verification.note: Sourced from the Junior Fastrack botany book, Biological Classification chapter (book pp.4-5), which prints the question and a model answer but NO star ranks and NO year citations. Only ONE source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this card, not merely pending: 'not checked' must never be read as 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The book prints 'Some fungi causes diseases' (grammar) and 'white spots on mustard leaves'; the standard name of the Albugo disease is white rust of mustard, which this card uses while keeping the book's phrase in brackets.

steps.label: Food
lines: Mushrooms, morels and truffles are common
steps.why: The direct food role comes first: these three named fungi are eaten as food, the simplest daily-life role to state.
common_mistakes: Naming only mushroom. Morels and truffles complete the listed edible fungi.
steps.memory_tip: Three edible names: mushrooms, morels, truffles.
steps.margin_note: One line with the three names is enough.

steps.label: Bread and beer
lines: Unicellular fungi like yeast are used in
steps.why: Yeast ferments sugar and releases carbon dioxide and alcohol: the gas raises bread dough and the alcohol makes beer — one organism, two products.
common_mistakes: Calling yeast a bacterium. Yeast is a unicellular fungus.
Writing yeast for curd. Curd is made by bacteria (Lactobacillus).
steps.memory_tip: Yeast: gas for bread, alcohol for beer.

steps.label: Antibiotics
lines: Some fungi, such as Penicillium, are used
steps.why: Penicillin, the first antibiotic, comes from the fungus Penicillium — the medical role of fungi in daily life.
common_mistakes: Writing Penicillium as a bacterium. It is a fungus (a mould).
steps.memory_tip: Penicillium the fungus gives penicillin the medicine — nearly the same word.
steps.margin_note: The genus name is the marked word.

steps.label: Diseases
lines: Some fungi cause diseases in plants and
wheat rust is caused by Puccinia;
white rust (white spots) on mustard leaves

lines.text: Food, bread and beer, antibiotics — and diseases.

steps.why: The role of fungi includes harm: fungi are also disease agents, and the two named plant diseases with their pathogens complete a balanced answer. (The book prints white spots on mustard leaves; the standard name of the Albugo disease is white rust.)
common_mistakes: Pairing the wrong pathogen: Puccinia — wheat rust; Albugo — white rust of mustard.
Writing only the useful roles. The syllabus answer includes the diseases.
steps.memory_tip: Puccinia on wheat, Albugo on mustard — pathogen before crop.
steps.margin_note: Two disease pairs plus the recap box close the answer.

insider_note: Four separate roles, one mark each — a paragraph about mushrooms alone earns one of the four.
